items.title: Unitree Reclaims the Spotlight with 18,000 Cumulative Bipedal Humanoids Produced
items.summary: Unitree has cumulatively produced approximately 18,000 bipedal humanoid robots as of July 2026. The company specifically excludes wheeled platforms or hybrid designs from its total count, focusing on purely bipedal models. This milestone comes after Unitree's record-breaking $904 million STAR Market IPO and puts pressure on rival AGIBOT in the competitive volume battle.
items.audio_script:
From Humanoids Daily, "Unitree Reclaims the Spotlight with 18,000 Cumulative Bipedal Humanoids Produced", Unitree has now cumulatively produced approximately 18,000 bipedal humanoid robots as of July 2026. This milestone marks a significant achievement in the company's production capacity and demonstrates its commitment to developing purely bipedal models.

The production of these 18,000 units was made possible through a combination of advanced manufacturing techniques and a robust research and development process. Unitree has been continually refining its design and production methods to improve efficiency and quality, resulting in a steady increase in output over the years. The company's focus on bipedal humanoid robots has allowed it to maintain a competitive edge in the market.

Unitree's record-breaking 18,000 units put pressure on rival AGIBOT in the competitive volume battle, as the company aims to solidify its position as a leading player in the AI and tech industry.

items.title: ROS Discourse General: Analyzing rosbags with LLMs and SQL + queryable Nav2 behavior trees
items.summary: Researchers at Pixel Robotics have developed an approach to analyzing ROS bags using Large Language Models (LLMs) and a database-based design, similar to MCP-rosbags + mcp-lab. They utilize the mcap-mcp-server software with SQL queries for fast analysis and efficient behavior tree log retrieval through Nav2 BT logging extensions. An agent skill is also shared to simplify setup, providing a useful resource for the community.
items.audio_script:
From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: Analyzing rosbags with LLMs and SQL + queryable Nav2 behavior trees". Researchers at Pixel Robotics have developed an approach to analyzing ROS bags using Large Language Models (LLMs) and a database-based design. They utilized the mcap-mcp-server software, which is similar to MCP-rosbags + mcp-lab, for fast analysis and efficient behavior tree log retrieval through Nav2 BT logging extensions. This was achieved by leveraging SQL queries, allowing users to efficiently query the logs. Additionally, an agent skill was shared to simplify setup, making this a useful resource for the community.

The researchers' approach enables fast and efficient analysis of ROS bags, which can be particularly beneficial for tasks such as behavior tree tuning and simulation optimization. By utilizing LLMs and SQL queries, users can quickly retrieve specific logs and analyze them in detail. The development of the agent skill also streamlines the setup process, making it easier for others to adopt this approach.

The development of this new method for analyzing ROS bags marks an important advancement in the field of robotics and artificial intelligence. With the increasing complexity of ROS bags, being able to efficiently analyze and query them is becoming increasingly essential for researchers and practitioners alike.

items.title: ROS Discourse General: Is this Embodied Agent project useless?
items.summary: The author spent 9 months working on an Embodied Agent project using ROS and VLM algorithms, building a simulation stack from scratch, integrating various packages, and creating a web application to configure the project. Despite completing the project with over 400 commits and 1000+ hours of work, the agent lacks realistic human-like understanding of its environment, relying solely on deterministic algorithms. The author believes that this is a major limitation, making the project feel useless and unsure if they should continue down this path.
items.audio_script:
From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: Is this Embodied Agent project useless?" This story highlights a recent finding from an individual's 9-month effort on an Embodied Agent project using ROS and VLM algorithms. The author built a simulation stack from scratch, integrated various packages, and created a web application to configure the project, culminating in over 400 commits and more than 1000 hours of work.

The project's findings indicate that despite these efforts, the agent lacks realistic human-like understanding of its environment, relying solely on deterministic algorithms. The author believes this is a major limitation, rendering the project ineffective and casting doubt on whether to continue down this path. 

This outcome underscores the ongoing challenges in developing intelligent agents capable of nuanced environmental interactions, highlighting the need for continued innovation and research in the field of artificial intelligence and robotics technology.

items.title: ROS Discourse General: Properly close windows processes, discussion about implementation
items.summary: Windows does not have a proper way to handle SIGINT, causing ungraceful shutdowns. The issue is with using `signal.SIGTERM` instead of `signal.CTRL_C_EVENT` on Windows, which is the correct signal to send for proper termination. A developer attempted to implement this change but encountered issues, including increased failures in CI runs and failed pull requests.
items.audio_script: From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: Properly close windows processes, discussion about implementation". A discussion has been taking place regarding the proper closure of Windows process windows on SIGINT signals, as the current method using `signal.SIGTERM` instead of `signal.CTRL_C_EVENT` is causing ungraceful shutdowns. The issue was identified and a developer attempted to implement a change by switching from `signal.SIGTERM` to `signal.CTRL_C_EVENT`, but encountered issues such as increased failures in Continuous Integration runs and failed pull requests, highlighting the complexity of implementing signal handling on Windows.

items.title: China racing ahead in autonomous car adoption, says new report
items.summary: China is the country most prepared for self-driving cars, ranking first due to massive robotaxi deployment, nearuniversal 5G coverage, and advanced regulations. The US follows with Waymo completing about 500,000 paid rides weekly. China has more than 17 million robotaxi rides recorded, with Apollo Go operating fully driverless vehicles without a safety driver, and 96% of the population covered by 5G.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, "China racing ahead in autonomous car adoption, says new report," a recent study has found China is now the country most prepared for self-driving cars. According to the report, massive robotaxi deployment, nearuniversal 5G coverage, and advanced regulations have contributed to this ranking. Waymo has been completing approximately 500,000 paid rides weekly in the US. In contrast, China has seen over 17 million robotaxi rides recorded, with several companies operating fully driverless vehicles without a safety driver. Additionally, 96% of China's population is covered by 5G networks, allowing for seamless communication and data exchange between autonomous vehicles and infrastructure.

items.title: Robotics roadmaps from around the world
items.summary: Roboticists and policymakers are developing country-specific roadmaps to advance robots' capabilities, interact with the physical world, and address societal needs. These roadmaps, led by academia, industry, and government entities, aim to guide innovation and investment in robotics. Examples include the US National Robotics Roadmap, the European Union's ADRA Strategic Research Agenda, and China's Made in China 2025 initiative, which prioritize areas such as collaborative robots, physical AI, and technological sovereignty.
items.audio_script: From Robohub, "Robotics roadmaps from around the world", a collection of country-specific plans is being developed by roboticists and policymakers to advance robotics capabilities, interact with the physical world, and address societal needs. These roadmaps, led by academia, industry, and government entities, aim to guide innovation and investment in robotics, highlighting priority areas such as collaborative robots, physical AI, and technological sovereignty. The US National Robotics Roadmap, the European Union's ADRA Strategic Research Agenda, and China's Made in China 2025 initiative are notable examples, prioritizing collaboration between industry and academia, investing heavily in research and development, and focusing on long-term strategies to drive robotics innovation.

items.title: The 370-billion-dollar race: How integrated design can help humanoid manufacturers succeed in a rapidly growing market
items.summary: Humanoid robots are poised to revolutionize manufacturing with unprecedented flexibility, navigating cluttered spaces and handling diverse products. A $370 billion market is expected to emerge by 2040 if progress continues at current rates. However, technical challenges, such as coordinating dozens of articulated joints and simulating complex systems, must be overcome. Siemens Xcelerator offers a solution, integrating design, simulation, and manufacturing workflows to eliminate systemic design obstacles.
items.audio_script:
From The Robot Report, "The 370-billion-dollar race: How integrated design can help humanoid manufacturers succeed in a rapidly growing market." This story highlights how Siemens Xcelerator is addressing the technical challenges hindering humanoid robot development by integrating design, simulation, and manufacturing workflows to eliminate systemic design obstacles.

According to reports, Siemens Xcelerator offers a comprehensive solution by seamlessly coordinating dozens of articulated joints through advanced simulations and modeling techniques. By streamlining design processes, manufacturers can overcome the complexities associated with simulating complex systems and optimize production workflows for more efficient and effective human-robot collaboration. This integrated approach enables humanoid robots to navigate cluttered spaces and handle diverse products with unprecedented flexibility.

As the market is expected to reach $370 billion by 2040 if progress continues at current rates, this breakthrough solution positions Siemens Xcelerator as a key player in addressing the technical hurdles facing the rapidly growing humanoid robot industry.

items.title: Protection Levels for Vision-Based Pose Estimation
items.summary: A new algorithm for computing protection levels in vision-based pose estimation is presented, which provides probabilistic bounds on pose error under undetected faults. The algorithm covers all six degrees of freedom of the aircraft pose directly and analyzes the effect of measurement redundancy, pixel-level prediction uncertainty, and runway distance on protection levels. The results demonstrate tradeoffs in the protection levels on an illustrative runway example.

items.title: The Impact of Operational-Data Fidelity when Assessing Safety-Critical Autonomous-Vehicle Software
items.summary: Insufficiently detailed operational data can undermine safety claims in autonomous vehicle software assessments, despite conservative analysis. This limitation can lead to dangerously optimistic reliability claims. The lack of detail can result from incomplete or inconsistent data, which can be problematic for assessing the robustness of reliability claims. Conservative Bayesian inference techniques are extended to investigate the impact of data fidelity on assessments.

items.title: Navigating the Proximity-Safety Balance: Constraint Decomposition for Human Following in Pedestrian Crowds
items.summary: Researchers have developed a method for human-following in pedestrian crowds, which navigates the proximity-safety balance by decomposing the task into sparse reward and independent cost constraints. This approach allows for explicit control over the trade-off between staying close to the target and navigating safely among surrounding pedestrians and obstacles. The method also incorporates prediction uncertainty of human motions to enhance safety under unpredictable conditions. Extensive experiments demonstrate its effectiveness in both in-distribution and out-of-distribution settings.

items.title: Whole-Body Planning for Humanoids Navigating Confined Spaces via Self-Collision Avoidance References
items.summary: Whole-body planning for humanoids navigating confined spaces requires integrating self-collision avoidance into a reachability-constrained formulation. A three-stage framework formulates kinematic path planning directly over kinematically reachable rigid-body volumes, synthesizing volume-informed guides that guide a full-order trajectory optimizer over long horizons. This approach achieves restricted confinement ratios (C_r < 1.5) and generates feasible trajectories across complex foot and hand contacts, while a learned policy successfully tracks these plans under domain randomization.

items.title: FACT: Failure-Aware Causal Training for World-Action Models
items.summary: FACT, a causal World-Action Model, predicts future video and task progress conditioned on the executed action. This allows failure rollouts to supervise action consequences, turning bad actions into valid future targets rather than being discarded. Extensive experiments show that FACT outperforms existing baselines, improves with failure data, and reduces success-biased future hallucination under bad actions.

items.title: A Neural Network Based Teleoperation for Remote Controlled Vehicles
items.summary: A neural network-based teleoperation framework is proposed to address technical bottlenecks in direct vehicle control, including communication latency and uncertainty compensation. The system integrates the Wave Variable approach for passive stability under stochastic delays and an adaptive Radial Basis Function Network (RBFN) for active compensation of vehicle-specific uncertainties. Simulation benchmarks demonstrate that the RBFN achieves superior robustness against unmodeled disturbances while requiring orders of magnitude less execution time than other control methods. Hardware-in-the-loop experiments validate the system's practical feasibility, safety, and robust trajectory tracking under physical road uncertainties.

items.title: Real-World Cooperative Bimanual Dexterous Grasp of Large Objects from Single-View Observations
items.summary: Researchers developed a real-world cooperative bimanual grasping framework that enables the synthesis of executable bimanual grasps from single-view inputs, reducing dependence on complete 3D object models. The approach includes a multimodal dataset, a Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model (DDPM)-based module that generates joint-level grasp configurations, and an execution strategy that integrates motion planning with online grasp refinement. Experiments demonstrated high success rates across unseen objects with varying geometries and poses using a dual-arm robot.

items.title: Hip Energized Monopedal Hopping
items.summary: Researchers have developed a new stepping strategy for monopeds, utilizing reaction torques to counteract energetic losses from damping and increase pitch stabilization torque. This results in a user-specified balance between steady-state fore-aft speed and apex height. The strategy has been validated through simulation studies on a generic 5-link biped and physical experiments on the Penn Jerboa, achieving speeds of up to 1.77 m/s (8.85 leg lengths/s).

items.title: PBD-AG: Persistent Baseline-Delta Active Graphs with Uncertainty-Aware Inspection for Long-Horizon Service Robots
items.summary: PBD-AG presents a persistent baseline-delta active graph framework for long-horizon service robots that autonomously builds structural baseline and inspects fixtures to ground hierarchical object beliefs. The framework maintains reliability-weighted object states over geometry, semantics, identity, existence, and support relations. Simulation experiments show higher aggregate coarse-fixture F1 scores than capability-matched controls, as well as stronger identity continuity and event recall. PBD-AG integrates with onboard sensing, providing a traceable world model for long-horizon robotic applications.

items.title: Lost in Reconstruction: Aligning Action Representations with Language in Vision-Language-Action Models
items.summary: Researchers introduced SALT, a Semantically ALigned action Tokenizer, to improve language-conditioned control in vision-language-action models by aligning action representations with language. This approach enhances verb-specialized codes while maintaining reconstruction fidelity, leading to 71.9% average success in SimplerEnv, compared to 42.7% and 31.2% for other methods.
